To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of the EDFM implementation is reduced in the presence of SA and that the performance of radially symmetric PSF systems is less affected by SA than radially asymmetric systems.
EDFM with radially symmetric PSF and model-based restoration algorithms is more accurate and robust to spherical aberration and signal-to-noise degradation.
the use of model-based computational methods with radially symmetric PSF designs is a promising approach to achieving EDFM performance in the presence of depth induced SA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the robustness of EDFM to spherical aberration and the effectiveness of EDFM for the imaging of biological specimens.
the evaluation of EDFM performance in the presence of depth induced SA and noise, using a variety of phase masks, and computational algorithms.
developing an understanding of the impact of spherical aberration, in terms of the PSF’s robust design, on the performance of EDFM.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of EDFM with wavefront encoding is limited by the SA induced by the depth of focus.
the use of a model-based reconstruction method is essential to achieve accurate structural fidelity and positioning of beads at depths of 10 μm or greater, in the presence of SA.
EDFM, with model-based computational reconstruction, is effective for achieving the conventional resolution limit in the presence of depth-dependent SA and noise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EDFM is effective in the presence of depth-dependent aberrations and noise when a radially symmetric PSF is used in conjunction with an appropriate computational method.

, in the presence of SA and noise, EDFM can achieve a resolution limit comparable to conventional microscopy, but the quality of the final image will be dependent on the PSF design, the computational method, and the imaging application.
, in the presence of depth induced SA, the use of radially symmetric PSF designs, coupled with model based computational reconstruction methods, is the preferred approach for EDFM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a given phase mask design, the PSF’s robust performance to SA is a critical parameter in determining the overall effectiveness of EDFM.
the PSF of the microscope system should be radially symmetric to achieve the highest structural fidelity in images restored using computational reconstruction methods.
EDFM is an effective tool for high-resolution microscopy imaging at depths where the conventional microscope is not effective, provided a model-based reconstruction method is used.
